ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Question: 437
A school class is going on a class trip, and a vote is being taken of where the class wants to go. The school expects that half of the students would want to go to Disney World, while the other half would want to go to visit Washington, DC Despite these expectations, only 42 students wanted to go to Washington, DC, while twice as many wanted to go to Disney World. Which of the following correctly identifies the chi-square statistic?

method.method_draft: Compute the statistic from the wording. From the text, 42 students chose Washington, DC and twice as many chose Disney World, so Disney World has 84 votes and the total is 126. The expected split is half and half, so each expected count is 63. Apply chi-square goodness-of-fit: χ² = Σ((observed − expected)^2 / expected). For Washington: (42−63)^2/63 = 441/63 = 7. For Disney World: (84−63)^2/63 = 441/63 = 7. Add the contributions: 7 + 7 = 14.
method.CoT_raw: The image shows a chi-square table with two categories: Washington and Disneyland/Disney World. It lists expected counts of 63 and 63, actual counts of 42 and 84, deviations of -21 and 21, squared deviations of 441 and 441, and contributions of 7 and 7. From the wording: 42 students chose Washington, DC, and twice as many chose Disney World, so Disney World has 84 votes and the total is 126. With an expected half-and-half split, each expected count is 63. The chi-square statistic is ((42 - 63)^2 / 63) + ((84 - 63)^2 / 63) = 441/63 + 441/63 = 7 + 7 = 14.
